title: Soak & Burst Autoscaling Harness for Dedicated Capacity (tokens/sec, p95 regression detection)
creator: Marco Reyes
description: Build a repeatable, observable harness for Dedicated capacity that runs long-duration soak tests plus controlled burst + steady-state autoscaling scenarios. Measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, error budgets, KV cache warm-up behavior, and detect regressions vs baseline. The harness must be runnable in CI and as a standalone job against staging and dedicated clusters, and emit metrics to Prometheus and Redwood Console for alerting and regression dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Soak run: 6 hour steady-state at target load with token/sec and p95 logged every 30s
Burst pattern: 3x baseline QPS for 60s every 10 minutes for the first hour, then return to steady-state
Autoscaler exercise: replicas scale up/down deterministically in response to sustained CPU/KV cache miss signals within configured SLOs
Regression detection: alert if p95 increases by >15% vs baseline or tokens/sec drops by >10% for two consecutive minutes
Reports: Generate a single HTML/JUnit-like artifact with time series, anomalies, and summary metrics linked to the test run
tasks: Design burst + steady-state scenarios and parameterize (baseline QPS, burst multiplier, burst duration, soak duration)
Implement load generator adapters for k6 and our internal loadgen to emit token counts per request
Instrument harness to publish Prometheus metrics: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p95_latency_ms, errors, kv_cache_hit_rate
Wire harness alerts into regression-detector job and Redwood Console dashboard
Run full soak against staging dedicated cluster and capture baseline; iterate on thresholds
Document runbook and CI pipeline job for nightly regression runs
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Infra, Serving Runtime, and Observability. Agreed to use k6 for burst scenarios and internal loadgen for sustainable token accounting.
2026-03-04: Prototype harness emits tokens/sec and p95 to Prometheus. Observability team suggested canonical metric names: rw_tokens_per_sec, rw_p95_ms, rw_kv_hit_rate.
2026-03-06: First staging soak (2 hours) completed. Observed KV cache warm-up impact—p95 spiked 25% in first 8 minutes. Decided to add a warm-up phase (10 minutes at 30% load) to baseline runs.

2026-03-08: Regression-detector rules drafted. Thresholds proposed: p95 > 15% vs baseline OR tokens/sec drop > 10% for >= 120s triggers investigation ticket. PM asked for one-week false-positive review window before auto-blocking releases.
2026-03-09: Design review with PM and SRE. SRE requested adding node-level metrics (GPU_util, host_cpu, memory) to correlate scale events. Assigned ENG-4855 to extend exporters.
2026-03-10: Ran full 6-hour soak in staging with final scenario parameters. Captured artifacts and created preliminary summary. Next: run against dedicated-qa and tune autoscaler policy parameters.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Chose k6 for burst patterns because it supports real-time ramping and JS-based scenario control; internal loadgen used for token accounting accuracy.
Decision to add 10-minute warm-up to reduce KV cache cold-start noise in results; tradeoff is slightly longer test runtime but more stable baselines.
Regression thresholds set conservatively (15% p95) to avoid noisy alerts; PM to review after 2 weeks of nightly runs to tighten thresholds if false positives are low.
Opted to emit metrics to Prometheus + Redwood Console instead of pushing boxed artifacts only; helps triage and correlates with existing dashboards.
Will not block releases automatically on first observed regression — initial runs create tickets and require manual triage per PM request.
review_feedback: PM - Lina Chen: Ensure reports include per-model breakdown (large vs small models) so customers can map regressions to model families.
SRE - Omar Haddad: Add autoscaler event logs and include decision timestamps in artifacts to debug flapping during burst windows.
Design - Priya Nair: Suggested a simple UI mock for the soak-run summary page in Console (timeline + top 3 anomalies).
Runtime - Hannah Kim: Noted that quantized model variants show different warm-up patterns; recommend tagging runs with model_variant metadata.
next_steps: ENG-4855: Extend node exporter to include GPU_util and host-level metrics (assigned to SRE)
Run dedicated-qa 6-hour soak (target date 2026-03-15) and evaluate regression-detector false-positive rate
Add model_variant metadata and per-model aggregation to the harness (follow-up PR in rw-load-tests)

Finalize acceptance criteria and move ticket to In Review once dedicated-qa soak completes
